lines.text: He builds a see through cylinder head and then feeds the engine a can of Monster Energy.
He drills and sands a block of clear plastic and even cuts a head gasket out of plywood.
Monster is mostly water and sugar so the real question is what all that sugar does once it burns inside an engine.
beats: ai:white sugar crystals glowing and melting inside a small engine combustion chamber macro

lines.text: And look at that flame through the clear head.
Then the exhaust smells sweet because the sugar is caramelizing on the hot metal like burnt candy.
beats: ai:sugar melting and caramelizing into brown syrup on red hot metal macro

lines.text: And after just a few minutes the clear head is gummed up and the clean valves already have carbon which shows how fast sugar builds up.
So he puts the real head back on and drips in most of the can.
And the engine barely runs and even spits fire back out of the carburetor.
The compression reads just 50 psi and the head comes out black because sugar burns into hard carbon that sticks to everything.
So would you give your engine an energy drink?
